reconcile.note: Gill assigns Deuteronomy's own-sin rule to human courts while reading Adamic death in Romans 5 as a judgment God alone administers, keeping the two in separate spheres.

discrepancy.note: Paine calls the doctrine that God visits the sins of the fathers upon the children contrary to every principle of moral justice.

quotes.text: God 'visits the sins of the fathers upon the children'. This is contrary to every principle of moral justice
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason (1794), Part I.

sides.snippet: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin.
sides.verseText: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin.

sides.snippet: as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin; and so death passed to all men, because all sinned.
sides.verseText: Therefore, as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin; and so death passed to all men, because all sinned.
